Export a Date Range of Cases to an Encrypted Export File

Source: R/import_export_export.R
episodic_cases_export.Rd

Writes this instance's own cases with a sample date from from to to into one encrypted, signed file that another EpiSODIC instance imports with episodic_cases_import(). The file is safe to keep in a public place (a public bucket, a shared drive, a Git repository): without a recipient's key it reveals nothing beyond its own size, and without your signing key nobody can forge or alter it. It works headless, from Rscript or a scheduled job, with no dashboard.

Usage

episodic_cases_export(
  db_path = Sys.getenv("EPISODIC_DB", unset = NA),
  from,
  to,
  file,
  recipients = NULL,
  signing_key = Sys.getenv("EPISODIC_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY", unset = NA),
  passphrase = NULL,
  fields = NULL,
  pc_characters = NULL,
  episodic_config_path = Sys.getenv("EPISODIC_CONFIG", unset = NA)
)

Arguments

db_path

The EpiSODIC database: a SQLite file or a MariaDB/MySQL DSN (see episodic_db_dsn_mariadb()). Defaults to the EPISODIC_DB environment variable.

from, to

The sample-date range, inclusive: Dates or "YYYY-MM-DD".

file

The path to write. An existing file is replaced, in one step, so a reader never sees half of it.

recipients

For public-key mode: one or more recipients' public encryption keys, each as its text or as the path of its .pub file.

signing_key

Your secret signing key, as its text or as the path of the file episodic_import_export_keygen() wrote. Defaults to the EPISODIC_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY environment variable.

passphrase

For passphrase mode: the passphrase. Give either recipients or passphrase, not both.

fields

The optional case columns to include (any of receipt_date, care_line, municipality, ward, specialism, pc, sex, age). NULL (the default) uses the configured export.fields. The required columns are always included.

pc_characters

Keep only the first this many characters of each postcode. NULL (the default) uses the configured export.pc_characters, which ships unset: postcodes as stored.

episodic_config_path

The configuration path. Defaults to the EPISODIC_CONFIG environment variable.

Value

Invisibly, a list with file, file_sha256, n_cases, fields, omitted_fields and export_id (the audit row).

Details

Two ways to encrypt, and the first is the one to use:

Public-key mode (recipients)

The file is encrypted to each recipient's public encryption key, and only their secret keys open it. Several recipients can share one file. The recipients cannot forge a file in your name, and replacing one recipient's key involves nobody else.

Passphrase mode (passphrase)

The file is encrypted with a key derived from a passphrase (scrypt, with a fresh random salt per file). Everyone who holds the passphrase can read every file, so changing it means coordinating every party at once. At least 16 characters.

In both modes the file is signed with your signing key, and an importer refuses it unless your public signing key is among the senders they have pinned.

What leaves the instance. Cases are exported as this instance stores them: one row per episode (see vignette("import-export")), with the institution as its stored SHA-1 hash, never the raw key. Cases this instance itself imported from a partner are never exported. Only the optional columns in fields are included; the others are left out of the file entirely, the file records which, and an importer receives them as not recorded (NA), never as a default value.

Every export is recorded in the database (episodic_export_event): when, by which host and account, the range, the columns, the recipients' key fingerprints, the signing key's fingerprint, the number of cases and the SHA-256 of the file. A failed export is recorded too.

See also

episodic_cases_import(), episodic_import_export_keygen(), vignette("import-export")

Examples

# \donttest{
db_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite")
episodic_run_cron(
  cases = episodic_synthetic_cases(
    start_date = as.Date("2025-01-01"), end_date = as.Date("2025-03-31")
  ),
  db_path = db_path,
  run_date = as.Date("2025-03-31")
)

sender <- episodic_import_export_keygen(tempfile())
receiver <- episodic_import_export_keygen(tempfile())
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".episodic")
episodic_cases_export(
  db_path = db_path,
  from = "2025-03-01",
  to = "2025-03-31",
  file = file,
  recipients = receiver$encryption_public,
  signing_key = sender$signing_secret
)
